Right triangle trigonometry: In a right triangle, sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan = opposite/adjacent (SOH-CAH-TOA). The special triangles give exact values: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = sqrt(2)/2, sin 60° = sqrt(3)/2, tan 45° = 1. Choose the ratio that uses the known side and the wanted side. Cofunctions satisfy sin θ = cos(90° - θ). Use inverse functions to find an angle.
Radians and the unit circle: A radian is the angle whose arc equals the radius, and 180° = π radians. Multiply by π/180 to convert to radians and by 180/π to convert to degrees. Arc length is s = rθ and sector area is (1/2)r²θ, with θ in radians. On the unit circle the point at angle θ is (cos θ, sin θ), so cos is the x-coordinate and sin is the y-coordinate. For example cos π = -1 and sin(π/2) = 1.
Trigonometric functions of any angle: For a point (x, y) on the terminal side with r = sqrt(x² + y²), sin θ = y/r, cos θ = x/r and tan θ = y/x. The signs follow the quadrants: all positive in I, sine in II, tangent in III, cosine in IV. Find the reference angle, take its value and apply the quadrant's sign. Coterminal angles differ by 360° (or 2π) and have the same values. Also sin(-θ) = -sin θ and cos(-θ) = cos θ.
Graphs of trigonometric functions: For y = A sin(B(x - C)) + D, the amplitude is abs(A), the period is 2π/B, the phase shift is C to the right and the midline is y = D. The range is D - abs(A) to D + abs(A). The graphs of sine and cosine have period 2π. Tangent has period π and vertical asymptotes at π/2 + nπ. A negative A reflects the graph over its midline.
Trigonometric identities: Key identities: tan θ = sin θ/cos θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, csc θ = 1/sin θ, and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Also sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and sin(a + b) = sin a cos b + cos a sin b. Use the Pythagorean identity to find one function from another, choosing the sign from the quadrant. To prove an identity, work on one side only, often by changing everything to sine and cosine.
Solving trigonometric equations: To solve a trigonometric equation, isolate the function, find the reference angle, and use every quadrant where the sign matches. Add multiples of the period for all solutions. Treat sin x or cos x as a variable and factor for quadratic-type equations, and never divide by a trig function, because that loses solutions. For sin 2x, solve for 2x on the doubled interval and then divide by 2. Equations like sin x = 2 have no solution.
